placements.title: the organization treats forgetting and removing knowledge as an active, directed governance act, not passive decay
placements.frame: Is this expression commanding the graph to discard a named artifact of knowledge, and what does the choice of target reveal about what the org no longer wants held?
placements.why: Both expressions are bare imperatives ('Forget the Quantum Widget Decision.' / 'Remove all knowledge about the PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration.') directing the deliberate excision of named knowledge artifacts. This is not a one-time fact to attach as evidence under some other theme — pass-2 confirms neither named target ('Quantum Widget Decision', 'PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration') exists anywhere in this graph, so there is no substantive leaf these could evidence. The recurring subject future envelopes could keep feeding is the practice itself: the org issuing directives to actively forget/remove specific knowledge, regardless of which artifact is named each time. Existing graph structure and strata are both empty ('none yet'), so no reuse is possible; this is the seed placement, left without a strata parent since nothing in the (empty) taxonomy is even close and forcing an ungrounded strata mint for two directives would be premature sprawl.
consulted: pass-2 resolutions confirming both phrases are 'new' — not present elsewhere in the graph
position pass grouping (KnowledgeErasureDirectives) as corroborating that both segments share one directional read
